home.faq_desc: The questions we hear most before people join.
home.faq_1_q: Who can attend the trainings, and is there a fee?
home.faq_1_a: Courses and webinars on IDEC Academy are free; once you register at no cost you can follow them at your own pace, and after completing at least 80% of the trainings you can download your certificate as a PDF. The audience is broad: managers and engineers in CBAM-covered sectors (iron and steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers), professionals doing corporate carbon footprint and sustainability reporting, academics and postgraduate students working on climate change and CCUS, and public sector specialists working on climate policy. For certificate programmes and technical workshops held outside the platform, terms may vary by programme.
home.faq_2_q: How can SMEs benefit from this project?
home.faq_2_a: What SMEs most often lack is the knowledge and capacity to measure their carbon footprint, and the project closes that gap on three fronts. Capacity: training on corporate carbon footprint accounting to ISO 14064-1, reporting embedded emissions under CBAM, and circular economy practice (reduce, reuse, recycle, recover). Technology: insight into carbon capture options and energy efficiency approaches without entering costly R&D. Finance: becoming able to meet green loan and incentive requirements through sustainability reporting. The payoff is concrete: anticipating CBAM costs in exports, cutting operating costs through energy and material efficiency, and becoming a preferred supplier in EU value chains.
home.faq_3_a: Yes. The centre combines academic expertise with field experience to offer facility-specific technical and strategic guidance: assessing which carbon capture technologies (amine-based systems, metal-organic frameworks, calcium looping) suit your plant, CBAM reporting processes and cost analysis, establishing a carbon footprint methodology compliant with ISO 14064-1, decarbonization roadmaps for energy-intensive sectors such as iron and steel, cement and aluminium, and circular economy and waste management. Scope and duration are set according to each organisation's needs; use the channels on the Contact page to send your request.
home.faq_more: Can't find the answer you need?
home.faq_4_q: What can I ask KarbonBot, and are my chats private?
home.faq_4_a: You can ask KarbonBot anything from carbon capture, storage and utilisation technologies to CBAM and EU regulation, from measurement and abatement methods to green finance — it sits in the bottom right corner of every page. On privacy: KarbonBot runs on a server that is physically separate and independent from the IDEC-TT data infrastructure. Your conversations are processed only on that server; your learning progress and personal data are never transferred to it. Even so, we recommend not typing commercially sensitive plant data into the chat and sending formal requests through the Contact page instead.
home.faq_5_q: How can we join the project as a partner or participant?
home.faq_5_a: There are four models depending on your organisation: technical implementation partnership for those offering a pilot site or developing technology in carbon capture, mineralisation or energy efficiency; strategic participation for organisations active in sector knowledge sharing and dissemination; training partnership for those shaping certification and staff training needs; and R&D collaboration for joint projects using the centre's laboratory and academic infrastructure. The process runs in three steps: a letter of intent stating where your organisation can contribute, a technical meeting with the centre's experts to define scope, and a protocol formalising the collaboration. To start, send your organisation details and proposal through the Contact page.
home.faq_6_q: Where do I start with calculating our carbon footprint?
home.faq_6_a: Start by setting your boundaries: which facilities are in scope, and which emission scopes you will account for. Scope 1 covers direct emissions (stacks, company vehicle fuel), Scope 2 purchased electricity, heat and steam, and Scope 3 the supply chain, raw materials, waste and transport — the last being the most critical for CBAM. Then gather a year of historical data: gas and electricity bills, fuel receipts, raw material and waste quantities. The calculation itself is a simple multiplication: activity data x emission factor. The final step is reporting the inventory and, where required, having it verified by an accredited body. Our TS EN ISO 14064-1 and CBAM reporting trainings are built precisely to help you run this process.

about.title: About Us
about.subtitle: Detailed information about the Industrial Decarbonization through Twin Transition project
about.project_vision_desc_1: The IDEC-TT project aims to create a sustainable and competitive industrial structure by realizing digital and green transformation simultaneously in Turkey's industrial sectors.
about.project_vision_desc_2: Sectoral transformation is supported with the KarbonBot artificial intelligence system, digital library, and training modules developed within the project.
about.problem_1: Lack of information and access for companies regarding carbon footprint measurement
about.problem_2: Digital transformation tools not being compatible and accessible to the sector
about.problem_4: Risk of being unprepared for international regulations like CBAM
about.solution_1_desc: Providing competitive advantage in exports for companies transitioning to low-carbon production
about.solution_2_desc: Access to investment and incentives through green financing mechanisms
about.solution_3_desc: Efficiency and cost advantage with Industry 4.0 and artificial intelligence solutions
about.solution_4_desc: Sustaining trade with the EU in a sustainable manner
about.team_subtitle: An interdisciplinary academic and technical team delivering the IDEC-TT project.
about.contact_uni_title: HOW TO REACH YEDITEPE UNIVERSITY TECHNOLOGY BASE?
about.transport_option_1: Close to Sabiha Gökçen Airport Metro Station
about.vision_headline: One roadmap that both digitalises and decarbonises industry
about.journey_desc: A company joining IDEC-TT goes through four steps. Each one is backed by a different component of the project.
about.journey_step_1_desc: Calculating the corporate carbon footprint and establishing how much each process emits.
about.journey_step_2_desc: Breaking the data down into hotspots and identifying energy efficiency and process improvement opportunities.
about.journey_step_3_desc: Applying low-carbon production, energy efficiency and circular material solutions on the ground.
about.journey_step_4_desc: Reporting and verification; meeting CBAM obligations and unlocking access to green finance.
about.mapping_title: Every problem is matched with an answer
about.mapping_desc: The four core problems of the project and the outcome that responds to each one.
about.why_desc: A significant share of Türkiye's emissions comes from industry — and since 2026, exporting to Europe means paying for those emissions.
about.chart_source: Source: TurkStat, Greenhouse Gas Emission Statistics, 2024. The energy figure also covers fuels burned in industry; industrial processes covers only emissions from chemical reactions in production.
about.cbam_subtitle: The carbon timetable for exports to the EU
about.cbam_step_1_desc: Reporting obligation only for embedded emissions in covered goods; no financial payment.
about.cbam_step_2_desc: On top of reporting, buying and surrendering carbon certificates became mandatory.
about.cbam_step_3_desc: Under the Updated Nationally Determined Contribution: 41% reduction against the reference scenario by 2030, peaking in 2038, net zero by 2053.
about.cbam_source: Sources: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (Regulation 2023/956) and Türkiye's Updated First Nationally Determined Contribution (2023).
about.components_title: Four tools that make the transition possible
about.components_desc: From access to knowledge to field application, the concrete outputs the project offers companies.
about.component_1_desc: An AI assistant fed by project resources, answering carbon management questions in Turkish.
about.component_2_desc: An open archive bringing together regulation, technology and good practice examples.
about.component_3_desc: Free, certified online courses and webinars delivered through IDEC Academy.
about.component_4_desc: One-to-one guidance helping companies build a roadmap for their own production processes.
about.closing_desc: Get in touch to join the project, take a course or start a collaboration.
about.total_caption: Türkiye's total greenhouse gas emissions in {{year}}. More than an eighth of that comes directly from industrial processes.
about.scope_title: The six product groups covered by CBAM
about.scope_subtitle: Which goods fall in scope when exporting to the EU, and how exposed is Türkiye?
about.scope_steel_desc: Rebar, pipes, flat products, fasteners. The largest in-scope item in Türkiye's exports to the EU.
about.scope_aluminium_desc: Unalloyed aluminium, bars, wire and sheets. Felt through automotive and construction supply chains.
about.scope_cement_desc: Clinker, portland and white cement. Among the most carbon-intensive groups per unit produced.
about.scope_fertiliser_desc: Ammonia, nitric acid and nitrogen fertilisers. Directly affects agricultural input costs.
about.scope_electricity_desc: Cross-border electricity trade. Volume between Türkiye and the EU is low relative to other items.
about.scope_hydrogen_desc: Pure hydrogen production. Limited volume today; a forward-looking heading for green hydrogen investment.
about.scope_source: Product groups are defined in the annex to EU Regulation 2023/956. Exposure levels are a qualitative assessment based on weight in Türkiye's exports to the EU, not a numerical share.

register_page.consent_modal_title: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Notice
register_page.consent_modal_body:
IDEC-TT Platform — Personal Data Processing Notice

1. DATA CONTROLLER
The data controller processing your personal data within the IDEC-TT project is Yeditepe University. Address: Sanayi Mah. Teknopark Bulvarı 7C Blok, Kurtköy - Pendik / İstanbul, Turkey.

2. PERSONAL DATA COLLECTED
During registration: full name, e-mail address, phone number, profession/title (individual membership), company name, tax ID and sector (corporate membership). Data generated during platform use: courses watched, watch durations, progress status.

3. DATA STORAGE AND SECURITY
Your personal data and learning progress records are stored in encrypted form exclusively on IDEC-TT infrastructure servers. Data is not shared with or sold to third parties. The KarbonBot AI assistant featured on the platform runs on a physically separate, independent server from the IDEC-TT data infrastructure. Conversation content is processed only on that server and your personal data or learning progress is never transferred to the KarbonBot server.

4. PURPOSE OF PROCESSING
a) Delivery and personalisation of training services,
b) Progress tracking and certificate generation,
c) Platform security,
d) Compliance with legal obligations.

5. RETENTION PERIOD
Your personal data is retained for the duration of your active membership and for 3 years after account deletion. Data subject to legal requirements is retained for the period specified in applicable legislation.

6. YOUR RIGHTS
Under the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698, you have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict processing of, and object to the processing of your data. To exercise these rights, contact us at idectt@yeditepe.edu.tr.

7. COOKIE POLICY
The platform uses only essential session cookies. No analytics or advertising cookies are used.

By accepting this notice, you give explicit consent to the processing of your personal data under the terms described above.
